t: The Mutapa Empire was a Shona state between the Zambezi and Limpopo, founded c. 1430 as Great Zimbabwe declined.
Its gold, traded via Swahili merchants at ports such as Sofala, tied the African interior to the Indian Ocean economy.
Succession disputes, Portuguese meddling and the rise of the Rozvi broke its power, though a remnant survived until 1917.
dyk: In 1561 the Jesuit Gonçalo da Silveira briefly converted the reigning Mwene Mutapa to Christianity, only to be killed at the royal court soon afterwards.
ev: Nyatsimba Mutota traditionally founds the state on the northern Zimbabwe plateau
Jesuit Gonçalo da Silveira converts the Mwene Mutapa and is then killed at court
A large Portuguese expedition under Francisco Barreto fails, largely through disease
Gatsi Rusere cedes mining rights to the Portuguese in return for military help
The Portuguese depose Kapararidze and install Mavura as a vassal ruler
The Rozvi under Changamire Dombo supplant Mutapa authority across the plateau
The Portuguese suppress the last reduced Mutapa kingdom in the Zambezi valley
